issue.title: SEV3: registry audit batching reads withdrawal history before locking candidate rows

review.reviewBody:
## Adversarial Review — Gemini (gemini-reviewer-lacey)

> Reviewer: gemini · Gemini 3.8 Flash (High) · none

## Summary

This PR addresses a concurrency race condition in worker-class deployment drift reconciliation under PostgreSQL `READ COMMITTED` (LAC-2089). Previously, `reconcile_seed_drift` fetched audit histories for candidate classes before acquiring per-row locks on those candidates, creating a window where an operator model withdrawal could be overridden by an earlier snapshot or a newly created class could lack an audit history entry.

The change locks candidate rows in deterministic lexicographical order (`sorted(seed)`) using `cfg.get_worker_class(..., for_update=True)` before calling `_audit_histories`, and reuses the locked row envelopes in the subsequent reconciliation loop. Concurrency edge cases around absent seed candidates, inactive rows, and missing classes are correctly guarded without deadlocks or unhandled exceptions. The accompanying tests in `modules/worker-pool/test/test_worker_class_deploy.py` use deterministic monkeypatching to verify both the pre-lock withdrawal boundary and the post-audit queue boundary. No blocking defects, security vulnerabilities, or contract drifts were found.

## Blocking issues

- None.

## Non-blocking issues

- **Redundant Ownership Column Checks in Candidate Comprehension**
  - **File:** `modules/worker-pool/lib/python/cwp_dispatch/worker_class_deploy.py`
  - **Lines:** `335-338`
  - **Problem:** In `reconcile_seed_drift`, the comprehension `candidates = {name: cfg.get_worker_class(conn, name, include_ownership=True, for_update=True) for name in sorted(seed)}` requests ownership metadata for every seed item, immediately after projecting governed classes on line 332. Each call with `include_ownership=True` invokes `_reg.ensure_apx_registry_columns(conn)` inside `get_worker_class`, performing schema column inspection queries on each iteration even though `reconcile_seed_drift` only consumes `row["spec"]` and `row["status"]`.
  - **Why it matters:** While `ensure_apx_registry_columns` is idempotent, repeatedly querying PRAGMA table information for every candidate class adds unnecessary database overhead during deploy drift reconciliation.
  - **Recommended fix:** Pass `include_ownership=False` to `get_worker_class` when populating `candidates` since ownership metadata is not evaluated by `reconcile_seed_drift`, or hoist a single `_reg.ensure_apx_registry_columns(conn)` call before the comprehension.
- **Audit History Query for Inactive Candidate Classes**
  - **File:** `modules/worker-pool/lib/python/cwp_dispatch/worker_class_deploy.py`
  - **Lines:** `338-341`
  - **Problem:** The audit history batch call `histories = _audit_histories(conn, {name for name, row in candidates.items() if row is not None})` includes all non-null candidates, while immediately below in the loop at line 349 the code executes `if row is None or row["status"] != "active": continue` and skips drift processing for inactive rows.
  - **Why it matters:** If a candidate worker class exists in `worker_classes` but has `status != "active"` (e.g. retired), its revision snapshots and audit history are fetched from `worker_class_audit` and parsed into memory only to be discarded without being read.
  - **Recommended fix:** Filter the candidate name set passed to `_audit_histories` to only include active classes via `{name for name, row in candidates.items() if row is not None and row.get("status") == "active"}`.

## Suggested fixes

1. In `modules/worker-pool/lib/python/cwp_dispatch/worker_class_deploy.py:335-338`, pass `include_ownership=False` in `cfg.get_worker_class` to avoid redundant column introspection per candidate class during lock acquisition.
2. In `modules/worker-pool/lib/python/cwp_dispatch/worker_class_deploy.py:338-341`, filter `{name for name, row in candidates.items() if row is not None and row.get("status") == "active"}` before calling `_audit_histories` to avoid loading audit trails for retired classes.

## Verdict

Comment only

nonBlocking.title: Redundant Ownership Column Checks in Candidate Comprehension
nonBlocking.finding: Candidate locking requested unused ownership metadata and repeated schema column inspection for every seed item.
nonBlocking.action: Set include_ownership=False while retaining for_update=True and sorted candidate locking. Extended query-trace coverage to reject ownership schema inspections during presence-only drift reconciliation. The sibling reconcile_seed_delta call retains ownership metadata because it evaluates local overrides.

nonBlocking.title: Audit History Query for Inactive Candidate Classes
nonBlocking.finding: Audit histories were fetched for retired candidates whose drift processing immediately skips them.
nonBlocking.action: Filter the post-lock audit batch to non-null active candidates. Extended the existing missing/retired presence-drift test to assert no audit-history query occurs while preserving existing reported presence drift and unchanged rows.
